newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy budget clears major hurdle, ERM awaits.
newsitem.headline: Italy budget clears major hurdle, ERM awaits.

text.p: Italy's controversial 1997 budget was approved by the lower house of parliament on Saturday, opening the way for the lira to return to the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM).

The austerity package, which is designed to tear 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) off next year's projected public sector deficit, was given the green light in the lower house after a month of steely debate.
"From today, tomorrow or the day after we will start negotiations for the lira's return to the ERM," Prime Minister Romano Prodi told reporters minutes after the vote.

The lira crashed out of the ERM in 1992 and its long-awaited re-entry is seen as a vital stepping stone towards Italy's goal of becoming a founder member of the planned single European currency, due to take off in 1999.

Prodi has said the budget, which is much more stringent than originally planned, will guarantee that Rome meets tough economic criteria laid down in the Maastricht Treaty for countries wishing to sign up to the Euro currency.
The package, which is hotly contested by Silvio Berlusconi's centre-right opposition bloc, now passes to the upper house (Senate) and must be turned into law by the end of the year.
Under the Italian constitution, both houses must ratify a bill before it goes on to the statute books.

Prodi's six-month-old centre-left coalition depends on the hardline Communist Refoundation for support in the lower house, but enjoys a clear majority in the Senate, which should ensure a smooth reading for the budget.
In a newspaper interview on Saturday, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi appeared to dampen expectations of an immediate lira return to the ERM fold.

"We (still) have to evaluate if...we will have to wait for ratification in both houses," he told La Stampa newspaper. "We haven't yet established when or at what level the re-entry will take place...now it's a question of entering the home straight and deciding the most opportune moment," he added.
Most analysts expect the lira to return to the ERM in time for the European Union's Dublin summit on December 13-14.
While almost all political parties in Italy support European monetary union, the opposition has condemned the way the 1997 budget sets about preparing the economy for the single currency.
They are particularly furious about plans to introduce a one-off Euro tax to levy some 11.5 trillion lire next year.
"This budget, which has been presented as a cure, will in fact bring misery," Antonio Marzano, a member of Berlusconi's Forza Italia party, told parliament on Saturday.
Opposition parties boycotted the final vote to protest at the package in a move criticised by Massimo D'Alema, leader of the largest coalition party, the Democratic Party of the Left.
"They counted on government parties falling out. But if we have passed a test like this it means we're capable of holding together in the future," he told parliament. $1 = 1,518
